LESSON: WRITING 2.3.2 WRITING PRACTICE

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Writing 2.3.2 Writing practice
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.3.2 Writing practice, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we make patterns?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.3.2 Writing practice together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
31

• Self-efficacy: The learner performs different activities in letter writing (modelling, colouring, and writing) and

confidently displays work done.

• Digital literacy The learner writes letters of the alphabet in lower case and upper case on a mobile phone, tablet or

laptop

Values:
• Social justice: The learner exercises freedom to express self and equity on sharing resources as they model and

colour.

● Peace: The learner together with others resolve differences responsibly that may occur when working together in

making patterns letters amicably in groups.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Personal hygiene: The learner clears the working space and washes hands after

the modelling experience

Link to other Learning Areas:

Creative Activities, the learner colours letters of the alphabet within borders while practising to write. Colouring is a

mostly done experience in Creative Arts..

Suggested Learning Resources:

Adapted course books, charts, board, digital device Signed audio visual story clips, books, Flash cards, online

resources,video games, charts, pictures, relevant digital devices
